title: Relief from wrong hole on a double green
question: Your ball comes to rest on a double green, but the wrong hole is directly in the line between your ball and the correct hole. What are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Play your shot as it lies, even if the hole is in the way.
Take free relief by moving your ball sideways, no closer to the hole, so the wrong hole isn't in your way.
Pick up your ball and replay your last stroke.
Ask another player to cover the wrong hole.

explanation: You're allowed free relief if the other hole interferes with your line. Place your ball at the nearest spot, not closer to the hole, where the wrong hole doesn't interfere.
imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer on a double green, placing his ball sideways away from a second hole that blocks his path to the flag.
imageAlt: Boy golfer on a double green, moving his ball away from the wrong hole.

issues: The golfer is addressing the ball with a natural, realistic right-handed posture.
Golfer is a teenage girl with natural proportions and correct ethnicity, light skin tone, yellow top, red trousers, and cap.
The golf putter is realistic in length, proportions, and head shape.
Exactly one golf ball is present and it is realistic in size and placement.
The green, flags, and holes are believable and consistent with a real putting green.
The background features are fitting for a golf course with no prohibited elements.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Depict the golfer actively placing the ball sideways away from the second hole (show explicit ball in hand, with clear ball movement away from the interfering hole), as per the illustration intent. Retain all other scene details.
